shortQuestions: The writer links the decorated trucks of today with the camel caravans of the past: just as camel drivers once decorated their camels with bells, beads and colourful cloth for long journeys on the trade routes, truck drivers now decorate their trucks, which have taken the place of camels as the carriers of goods across the land.

She is illustrating that truck art has regional styles: trucks from Peshawar, for example, are decorated with wooden carvings and particular motifs, while those from Rawalpindi are known for plastic work and reflective tape — each region has its own distinctive taste.

She shows that truck art is a skilled craft done by specialists — painters, carpenters, metal-workers and calligraphers — each working on a different part of the truck, so decorating a truck is a team effort of skilled artisans.

Truckers spend so much because the truck is their home and their pride for long periods; decoration expresses their personality, beliefs and love for their family and region, and a beautiful truck attracts more business and respect. It is also believed to bring good luck and protection.

In the 1940s trucks were decorated simply by the companies that built the bodies; gradually painters added floral designs and pictures. By the 1950s and 1960s, with the Bedford trucks, decoration became more elaborate with paintings, calligraphy, mirrors and metal work, and by the 1970s it had become a fully developed popular art form with competing workshops.

They are nostalgic because the old Bedford trucks were the first trucks on which truck art really flourished; they were strong, beautiful and easy to decorate, and they remind the drivers of the golden age of truck art.

Truck art has reached 'some kind of apogee' (the highest point) because it is now extremely elaborate and colourful, combining painting, calligraphy, mirror-work, steel and plastic decoration; it is famous all over the world, displayed in exhibitions and copied on objects, and has become a symbol of Pakistani popular culture.
activities: Sample composition — The Need of the Smart Phone: Today the smart phone has become a basic need rather than a luxury. First of all, it keeps us connected with family and friends through calls, messages and video chats. Moreover, it is a powerful tool for learning: students can search information, read e-books and attend online classes. In addition, it makes daily life easier — banking, shopping, navigation and booking tickets are only a touch away. However, it must be used wisely, because excessive use wastes time and harms health. Therefore, if used with balance, the smart phone is a blessing of modern technology. (Transitional devices: first of all, moreover, in addition, however, therefore.)

Pair activity guide: each student writes three similarities (e.g., same school, love of cricket, same favourite subject) and three differences (e.g., one likes reading, the other sports) about himself and his partner, then they compare and discuss which guesses were right or wrong, using comparison and contrast expressions (both, similarly, whereas, unlike).
